topic: Miscellaneous materials: asphaltic materials (asphalt, bitumen and tar), paints and varnishes, polymers

questions.q: 345. The ingredient which gives the desired colour to a paint is called
questions.explain: Pigments are finely ground solid particles that provide color, opacity, and some level of protection in paint.

questions.q: 346. The paints with white lead base are suitable for painting of
questions.explain: White lead base is excellent for wood because it is very durable and flexible, but it is rarely used on iron as it can promote corrosion compared to red lead.

questions.q: 347. The function of base of an oil paint is
options: to form the body of the paint
to reinforce the film of the paint after drying
to prevent penetration of paint to lower surfaces
questions.explain: The 'base' (like white lead or zinc oxide) provides the bulk or body of the paint and determines its character.

questions.q: 348. The vehicle used in case of enamel paints is
questions.explain: As per key but Enamel paint is essentially a mixture of pigment and varnish, which gives it a hard, glossy finish.

questions.q: 349. The main component of oil paint is
questions.explain: Oil paint requires a base/pigment, a vehicle (carrier), and a thinner (like turpentine) to be effective.

questions.q: 350. The pigment in paints gives
questions.explain: The primary role of the pigment is to provide color and hide the surface being painted.

questions.q: 351. Base pigments are used for
questions.explain: The base is a solid substance in a fine state of division and forms the bulk of a paint. It imparts durability and protects the surface from weathering.

questions.q: 352. Extenders used in paints for
questions.explain: Extenders (or fillers) are added to paint to increase its volume and make it spread more easily, which helps in reducing the overall cost.

questions.q: 353. The commonly used thinner in oil paints is
questions.explain: Both Naphtha and Turpentine are common thinners used to reduce the viscosity of oil-based paints for better workability.

questions.q: 354. The commonly used thinner in distempers
questions.explain: Distemper is a water-based paint, therefore water is used as the thinning agent to achieve the desired consistency.

questions.q: 355. Turpentine oil is used in paints as a
questions.explain: Turpentine oil acts as a solvent or thinner to make the paint thinner and more fluid for application.

questions.q: 356. The defect in painting over a smooth and glossy surface due to which paint does not stick to the surface, is known as
questions.explain: Blistering occurs when gas or moisture is trapped under the paint film, often because it fails to adhere to a smooth or glossy surface.

questions.q: 357. The base material for distemper is
questions.explain: Chalk (whiting) is the primary base material used in the preparation of distemper.

questions.q: 358. Distemper is a mixture of
questions.explain: Basic distemper consists of powdered chalk mixed with water and a binder (like glue/size).

questions.q: 359. Vehicle not used in paint is
questions.explain: Turpentine oil is a thinner, not a vehicle (carrier oil). Linseed, poppy, and tung oils are all common vehicles.

questions.q: 360. The paint highly resistant to fire is
questions.explain: Asbestos is naturally fire-resistant; hence, asbestos paint is used to protect surfaces from fire hazards.

questions.q: 361. The oily liquid in which base and pigment are dissolved to form a paint is called
questions.explain: The vehicle (or binder) is the liquid that holds the pigment and base in suspension and helps it adhere to the surface.

questions.q: 362. The base in a paint has the following function
options: it forms the body of the paint
it reinforces the films of the paint after it has dried
questions.explain: The base provides bulk, prevents shrinkage, and gives strength to the dried paint film.

questions.q: 363. The cracks in the painted surface extending throughout the thickness of the paint are caused due to
options: improper seasoning of the painted wood
too many coats of paint resulting in excessive thickness
questions.explain: Deep cracks can be caused by wood movement, chemical imbalances from driers, or mechanical stress from overly thick layers.

questions.q: 364. The small areas on painted surface enclosed by hair line cracks are called
questions.explain: Crazing refers to the formation of fine, shallow hairline cracks on the surface of the paint.

questions.q: 365. Lacquer paints are
options: are more durable compared to enamel paints
questions.explain: Lacquers are high-performance coatings often containing nitrocellulose and resins, known for their durability on metal surfaces.

questions.q: 366. Lacquer is
questions.explain: Lacquers are technically a type of spirit varnish that dries by evaporation of the solvent.

questions.q: 367. The solvent used in cement paints is
questions.explain: Cement paint is supplied in powder form and mixed with water for application.

questions.q: 368. Distemper is used on
options: plastered surfaces not exposed to weather
questions.explain: Distemper is not weather-resistant and is primarily used for interior walls (interior plastered surfaces).

questions.q: 369. The best primer used for structural steel/iron is
questions.explain: Red lead is the most effective primer for steel as it provides excellent corrosion resistance.

questions.q: 370. The commonly used cement in making cement paints is
questions.explain: White cement is used as the base for cement paints to allow for a wide range of pigment colors.

questions.q: 371. The paint used for automobiles is
questions.explain: Modern automobile finishes often use advanced oil-based paints for a smooth, durable finish.

questions.q: 372. Duco is the trade name for
questions.explain: Duco is a well-known brand of cellulose-based paint commonly used in the automotive industry.

questions.q: 373. The paint which gives illumination during night is called
questions.explain: Fluorescent or luminescent paints contain pigments that glow in the dark or reflect light intensely.

questions.q: 374. The function of a paint is
options: to increase the life of the surface
questions.explain: Paint serves both aesthetic (appearance) and protective (corrosion/weathering) functions.

questions.q: 375. The painting work is generally specified by
questions.explain: In engineering estimates, painting work is measured and specified in terms of surface area (square meters/feet).

questions.q: 376. The paints used in aircrafts are
questions.explain: Cellulose paints (lacquers) are used for aircraft because they dry very rapidly by evaporation and provide a hard, smooth, and flexible surface.

questions.q: 377. The defect in painting caused due to sliding of one layer of paint over another layer, is known as.
questions.explain: Alligatoring occurs when the top coat slides over the undercoat, creating a pattern of cracks resembling reptile skin.

questions.q: 378. The main constituent of varnish is
questions.explain: Resins (like amber, copal, or shellac) are the primary solid constituent of varnish that forms the protective film.

questions.q: 379. The varnish is essentially made of
questions.explain: Varnish consists of a resin dissolved in a solvent (and sometimes oil) to allow for application and film formation.

questions.q: 380. French polish is made by dissolving the resin
questions.explain: French polish is a type of spirit varnish made by dissolving shellac in methylated spirit.

questions.q: 381. Snowcem is
questions.explain: Snowcem is a well-known commercial brand name for waterproof cement-based paint.

questions.q: 382. The pigment used in paints for corrosive resistance is
questions.explain: Red lead (lead tetroxide) is highly effective at preventing the corrosion of iron and steel.

questions.q: 383. The pigment commonly used in the manufacture
questions.explain: Ambers (browns), Iron Oxide (reds/browns), and Lamp Black (blacks) are all standard pigments used to provide color to paint.

questions.q: 384. PVC controls in paint
questions.explain: Pigment Volume Concentration (PVC) affects nearly all physical properties of the paint film, including its sheen and strength.

questions.q: 385. PVC stands for
questions.explain: In the context of paint technology, PVC refers to the Pigment Volume Concentration.

questions.q: 386. Muller is concerned with
questions.explain: A muller is a tool (often stone) used to grind and mix pigments with a vehicle during paint preparation.

questions.q: 387. The cracks developed throughout thickness of paint due various reason is known as
questions.explain: Cracking involves deep breaks in the paint film that often expose the underlying surface.

questions.q: 388. The material generally not used as extender in paints is
questions.explain: Zinc white is a primary pigment (base), whereas silica, gypsum, and talc are inert materials used as extenders.

questions.q: 389. The following element of a paint is used as base, pigment as well as drier
questions.explain: Red lead is unique because it serves as a base, provides color (pigment), and acts as an oxidizing drier.

questions.q: 390. A prime coat is given to steel work
options: a mixture of linseed oil & red lead
questions.explain: The standard primer for steel is red lead mixed with linseed oil to prevent oxidation.

questions.q: 391. Stucco paints are suitable for
questions.explain: Stucco paints are specifically designed for external masonry surfaces like stone and brick.

questions.q: 392. The radiator of vehicles are pointed with
questions.explain: Bronze or aluminum paints are used for radiators due to their high thermal conductivity and heat resistance.

questions.q: 393. Inert filler / adulterant is used in paint to
questions.explain: Inert fillers (extenders) are used to bulk up the paint and make it more economical.

questions.q: 394. The most durable varnish is
questions.explain: Oil varnishes take longer to dry but are the most durable and weather-resistant.

questions.q: 395. Brilliant varnish is
questions.explain: Spirit varnishes (like French polish) dry quickly to a very high, brilliant gloss.

questions.q: 396. Bitumen is used for
questions.explain: Bitumen is a versatile hydrocarbon used for preventing water ingress and filling construction joints.

questions.q: 397. Asphalt is a mixture of
questions.explain: Asphalt is technically a combination of bitumen and mineral aggregates (sand/gravel).

questions.q: 398. Plastic asphalt is
options: a mixture of cement and asphalt
questions.explain: Plastic asphalt is typically a mixture of asphalt and cement used for patching and waterproofing.

questions.q: 399. When a bitumen is graded by 75/15, the figure 75 represents
questions.explain: In asphalt grading (e.g., Industrial Bitumens), the first number often denotes the softening point.

questions.q: 400. Bitumen paint renders
questions.explain: Bituminous paints are primarily used for their excellent protective and anti-corrosive qualities on ironwork.

questions.q: 401. Bitumen is
options: semi solid state is called mineral tar
questions.explain: In civil engineering and materials science, bitumen refers to a highly viscous, sticky black substance that changes form depending on its state and composition. It can be classified by its physical state: Solid state: Asphalt; Semi-solid state: Mineral tar; Fluid state: Petroleum.

questions.q: 402. Mastic asphalt is
questions.explain: The correct answer is all of the above. Mastic asphalt is a versatile construction material made of asphaltic cement and fine mineral aggregates that exhibits multiple protective properties: Water proof, Fire proof, and Elastic (thermoplastic and flexible, allowing it to adapt to normal movements in building structures).

questions.q: 403. Mastic asphalt is generally used for
questions.explain: Due to its impermeable nature, mastic asphalt is a standard material for Damp Proof Courses (DPC) and waterproof layer in buildings.

questions.q: 404. Bitumen is generally obtained form
questions.explain: Bitumen is a fractional distillation product of crude petroleum.

questions.q: 405. Bitumen may be dissolved in
questions.explain: Bitumen is chemically defined by its solubility in carbon disulphide ($CS_2$).

questions.q: 406. Plastic bitumen is generally used for
questions.explain: Plastic bitumen (bitumen mixed with fillers) retains its flexibility and is used to fill cracks in structures to prevent leakage.

questions.q: 407. Bitumen emulsion is
options: a liquid containing bitumen in suspension
questions.explain: An emulsion is a mixture where fine droplets of bitumen are suspended in water with the help of an emulsifying agent.

questions.q: 408. Bitumen felt is
questions.explain: Bitumen felt (rolls of fabric impregnated with bitumen) is used widely for both damp proofing and roof waterproofing.

questions.q: 409. Asphalt in obtained form
questions.explain: Asphalt is the heavy residue left after the distillation of certain types of crude petroleum.

questions.q: 410. Mastic asphalt is
questions.explain: Mastic asphalt is a durable, non-corrosive material often used in industrial flooring where chemical resistance is required.

questions.q: 411. The filler used in plastic bitumen is
questions.explain: Asbestos powder is commonly used as a filler in plastic bitumen to provide fiber reinforcement and stability.

questions.q: 412. Which one is correct with respect to bitumen?
questions.explain: Bitumen exists in various forms depending on its consistency and mineral content, from liquid to solid asphalt.

questions.q: 413. The union of two or more smaller molecule of same or different types with or without elimination of water is known as
questions.explain: Polymerization is the chemical process of combining small molecules (monomers) into a large network (polymer).

questions.q: 414. The degradation of polymers by disrupting the inter molecular bond is known as
questions.explain: Depolymerization is the reverse of polymerization, where the polymer is broken down into its original monomers or smaller fragments.

questions.q: 415. The natural rubber is obtained from the...........of the plant.
questions.explain: Natural rubber is processed from latex, a milky sap produced by various plants, most notably the Hevea brasiliensis tree.

questions.q: 416. Plastics are................materials.
questions.explain: Plastics are organic polymers, primarily derived from petrochemicals (carbon-based).

questions.q: 426. Tar is made by the distillation of
questions.explain: While coal tar is common, the book key identifies asphalt distillation as the source for this specific question context.

questions.q: 441. Distemper is used on
options: plastered surface not exposed to weather
questions.explain: Distemper is a water-based interior finish that is not suitable for surfaces exposed to rain or sun.

questions.q: 442. A good quality bitumen suitable for paving jobs should not indicated a loss in weight more than
questions.explain: When heated, high-quality bitumen should be stable with minimal loss of volatile components (typically <1%).
